observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a patterned carpet with a dark stain near the center. On the left a black handheld tool with a white side button and a brass nozzle tip is held pointed at the stain; on the right a person's hand grips a folded blue terry-cloth towel. A plume of white steam/vapor is present around the nozzle, the stain, and the cloth throughout. The grid-like carpet pattern and the stain remain in frame the whole time.
visible_changes: The black tool is not static: its brass nozzle tip shifts back and forth horizontally in repeated short strokes, alternately approaching and retreating from the stain region across the frames (e.g. leftward in early frames, rightward again later), so the tool's angle and the white button's position relative to the frame edges change.

The hand-held blue cloth also makes small positional adjustments, shifting slightly toward/away from the stain and changing its tilt/grip a little, though its overall location on the right stays roughly the same.
White steam/vapor continuously rises and swirls, varying in density and shape from frame to frame, partially veiling the cloth, the nozzle, and the stain.
The dark stain stays visible and roughly constant in size; no clear removal or growth is supported within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the device is, what it emits, and whether the cloth and tool are being used together or in sequence.
The cause of the stain and any cleaning outcome before or after this segment.
Whether the hand's motion is wiping, holding, or merely resting.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the small shifts in framing of the carpet grid are due to slight camera movement or only to the tool/cloth motion; background evidence is limited.
Whether the stain's appearance changes are real or just the result of steam obscuring it.
The exact purpose of the relative motion between the nozzle and the cloth.
